countermodel.algebra: H=Q[T]/(T+1)^2. Put u=T+1; 1,u are a basis, u^2=0, and Jac(H)=Q u is nonzero.
countermodel.ordinary_specht_modules: For (2), z=x_(2)=1+T=u. For (1,1), z=y_(2)=1-q^{-1}T=1+T=u. Both ordinary Specht modules equal the nonzero right ideal uH=Q u. Since uT=-u, both are one-dimensional simple modules. These are the only two partitions of 2.
countermodel.forms: The row-shape Specht is the rank-one row permutation module with form norm 1. The column Specht u in the regular row-permutation module has norm 1+q=0 at q=-1. A zero form quotient does not imply a reducible underlying module.
countermodel.conclusion: e<=n and nonsemisimplicity do not imply that some Specht module is reducible.

new50_relation: NEW50 supplies the genuine ordinary/Murphy module-and-form bridge, but neither asserts nor proves the false reducibility implication. NEW50 and the three checked actual NEW25 convention uses remain sufficient.
